identificationModule.briefTitle: Prospective Multicenter Study of the Genomic, Transcriptomic, and Biological Profile of Patients With Neuroblastoma
identificationModule.officialTitle: Protocollo Multicentrico Prospettico Studio Del Profilo Genomico, Trascrittomico e Biologico in Pazienti Affetti da Neuroblastoma / Prospective Multicenter Study of the Genomic, Transcriptomic, and Biological Profile of Patients With Neuroblastoma

descriptionModule.briefSummary:
This is an investigator-initiated, multicenter, prospective, non-profit study.

Patients who provide informed consent to participate will be asked to provide a peripheral blood sample, a fresh tumor tissue sample (obtained by biopsy), and/or a bone marrow sample.

All patients with neuroblastoma at diagnosis, with relapsed disease, or with refractory disease may participate, provided that the diagnosis and disease status are established by the treating physician in accordance with national clinical practice and by the participating study center.

Enrolled patients will be reported and registered by means of a paper-based notification form sent by email to the Coordinating Center, which will assign a unique identification code to each patient.

At the time of notification, clinical and treatment-related data will be collected using a paper-based Case Report Form (CRF).

Biological material (peripheral blood, bone marrow, and/or tumor biopsy samples) must be centralized at the Laboratory of Experimental Oncology Therapies, IRCCS Istituto Giannina Gaslini, Genoa, Italy, in accordance with the procedures described in the study protocol. Samples will be processed and analyzed as specified in the protocol.

The results of the initial analysis performed at CEINGE, Naples, will be communicated by the CEINGE Laboratory to the Coordinating Center. A multidisciplinary meeting will then be held with a panel of experts, including oncologists, biologists, pharmacists, and infectious disease specialists. Following this meeting, an individual report will be prepared for each patient.

The report will include the results of Whole Exome Sequencing (WES) or Cancer Gene Panel (CGP) analysis performed on the patient's DNA, together with any potential therapeutic recommendations based on the molecular alterations identified. The report will be sent to the physician responsible for the individual patient.

For patients who provide additional consent by signing the appropriate informed consent form, biological material may also be used for the following purposes:

i) Immunophenotyping, with particular focus on GD2 and B7-H3 expression in tumor biopsy samples and in neuroblastoma cells infiltrating the bone marrow;

ii) High-throughput screening of libraries comprising readily available anticancer drugs;

iii) Generation of in vitro and in vivo tumor models, including primary cell lines and spheroids in vitro, and murine models such as Patient-Derived Xenografts (PDX) and Cell Patient-Derived Xenografts (CPDX) at the Coordinating Center, as well as zebrafish models at San Martino-IST, Genoa, and/or Città della Speranza, Padua.

primaryOutcomes.measure: Molecular Profiling of Neuroblastoma to Identify Potential Therapeutic Targets
primaryOutcomes.description: The primary objective of the study is to characterize the molecular profile of neuroblastoma biopsy specimens collected at diagnosis, in cases of first-line treatment refractoriness or disease relapse. Whole-exome sequencing (WES) or comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) will be performed to identify somatic and/or germline mutations and genetic alterations in individual patients that may represent potential targets for specific drugs.
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: over a 3-year period, starting from the enrollment of the first patient in the study

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Identification of Targeted Therapeutic Strategies Based on Somatic Alterations
secondaryOutcomes.description: The secondary objective of the study is, whenever feasible, to suggest a targeted therapeutic strategy within a precision medicine approach, based on the identified somatic alterations.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: over a 3-year period, starting from the enrollment of the first patient in the study

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* All patients diagnosed with neuroblastoma at AIEOP centers.
* Signed informed consent/assent provided by the subject and/or their parents or legal guardians.
* Age 0 to ≤ 31 years.
* Life expectancy \> 3 months.
* Availability of fresh tumor tissue and/or bone marrow and peripheral blood samples.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Absence of signed informed consent/assent from the subject and/or their parents or legal guardians.
* Life expectancy \< 3 months.
eligibilityModule.studyPopulation: All patients with newly diagnosed, refractory, or relapsed neuroblastoma referred to AIEOP centers.
